transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Solutions), Evelyn Park (Crimson Head of Security), Marcus Reed (CTO), Sofia Diaz (Infra)

Summary:
Crimson Labs is evaluating Redwood for inference hosting; primary concerns are encryption/KMS integration, audit logs and retention, SSO/SAML and RBAC for multiple teams, and deciding between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem). Customer asked for SOC2 and ISO evidence and a hands-on perf comparison using a small sample workload. Redwood AE/SE explained deployment modes, KMS options (bring-your-own KMS vs Redwood-managed), audit log retention, and suggested a pilot + SE benchmark.

Topics covered:
- Compliance: SOC2, ISO 27001 attestations and where artifacts live
- Identity: SSO / SAML, SCIM provisioning, RBAC granularity
- Crypto: KMS integrations, key rotation, HSM options, BYOK
- Auditability: request/response logging, token-level billing, retention windows, export formats
- Hosting modes: Hosted, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Private VPC / on-prem considerations
- Operational: rollouts, canaries, fallback policies, and emergency access procedures

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): "All right good afternoon everyone. We're recording this — thanks for taking the time. Quick intros? I'll kick off, Jordan Miles from Redwood, AE. Priya is our solutions engineer, Liam is here for sizing. Over to you folks at Crimson."
[00:15] Evelyn (Crimson): "Hi, Evelyn Park, head of security. Marcus Reed, CTO and Sofia — I handle infra. We wanted to focus on security and hosting so we can decide if hosted or dedicated or bringing it into our VPC is the right move."
[00:30] Priya (SE): "Great. Can I start with a high-level checklist? SOC2/ISO posture, identity (SSO/SAML + SCIM), encryption & key management, logging/audit retention, and data residency. Anything else to add?"
[00:40] Marcus: "Yeah also RBAC model — we have separate teams (research, ops, product) with different privileges. And we need to know how quickly we can failover or fallback if capacity hits limits; like can we fall back to smaller models automatically?"
[00:57] Priya: "Yes, routing/fallback is part of the platform. We can do policy-based routing — latency vs cost vs region. For RBAC, we expose role mapping via SAML groups and fine-grained route-level permissions."
[01:10] Sofia: "Quick Q on SAML — we use Okta. Do you support certificate rotation and metadata refresh without downtime?"
[01:18] Liam (Redwood): "We support metadata endpoints and can automate rotation; there is a short re-auth window but we've built session continuity to avoid blocking in-flight requests. In practice it's seamless if you use automatic metadata refresh."
[01:33] Evelyn: "On KMS, we need BYOK and hardware-backed keys; some of our regulators insist on keys never leaving our HSM. How does Redwood handle that for Dedicated and Private?"
[01:45] Priya: "Two paths — hosted: Redwood-managed KMS with envelope encryption, or BYOK with customer-managed keys in a cloud KMS (AWS KMS/CloudHSM, Google CMEK). For Private deployments you can mount customer HSM or use the customer's KMS endpoint — keys don't leave your VPC in that configuration. We also have integrations with HSM providers for on-prem HSMs."
[02:03] Marcus: "So in hosted mode if we bring our KMS, are decryption ops proxied through Redwood? Does the plaintext ever touch Redwood-managed machines?"
[02:12] Priya: "We use envelope encryption. The master key (customer KMS) decrypts the data encryption key which then is used locally on the inference node. For BYOK with Private, the master key calls are restricted to the customer's network. We can provide a flow diagram in the whitepaper."
[02:28] Jordan: "I'll attach that diagram — it shows envelope encryption, where the K E Y is stored and where the data key is used. Also have a short note on rotation and key lifecycle management."
[02:40] Sofia: "Alright, audit logs — what do you capture? We need full request/response traces for 90 days and an exportable format for our SIEM."
[02:50] Priya: "We emit request metadata and full request/response bodies subject to configuration. For PII workloads we recommend logging metadata only and using payload redaction. Logs are shipped to S3 (or your syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver) and we support configurable retention policies — default is 30 days for payloads, 90 days for metadata, but enterprise can extend that. Export is JSON lines, with timestamps and request IDs."
[03:15] Evelyn: "Is there an immutable tamper-evident log option? Some teams want append-only audit trails for compliance."
[03:22] Priya: "We can enable signed audit logs with HMAC and store a hash chain; it's an add-on feature on Dedicated/Private. We'll include documentation and an example verifier script."
[03:33] Marcus: "Data residency — we have EU users and some APAC entitlements. Can you pin customer workloads to specific regions?"
[03:41] Liam: "Yes, region pinning is supported. For Hosted we have region-specific endpoints and aware routing. For Dedicated you can reserve capacity in a specific region. Private gives you full control."
[03:53] Marcus: "What about model artifacts — if we upload a fine-tuned model, does it replicate across regions automatically? We want to avoid cross-border replication unless explicitly set."
[04:02] Priya: "Replication is opt-in. By default artifacts are stored in the region of the deployment. We can provide a policy to prevent cross-region sync."
[04:11] Evelyn: "SAML mapping and RBAC — can we tie model access to groups so research can only run inference on sandbox models, but product can access production endpoints?"
[04:20] Priya: "Yes — route-level RBAC. You can map Okta groups to roles and restrict model visibility and invocation rights. We support temporary elevated access via SSO for audits or emergency runs."
[04:32] Sofia: "On retention, we have a legal hold scenario — can we freeze logs and increase retention for specific time windows?"
[04:40] Priya: "Yes, legal hold is supported. You can pin retention per-object or per-tenant. There's an API to set holds and to export archived data."
[04:50] Jordan: "Quick qualification — what's your timeline and who is the procurement owner?"
[04:54] Marcus: "We want a pilot in the next 6 weeks and a procurement decision in Q3. Procurement contact will be Handled by me and legal will step in once we have SOC2 + ISO artifacts."
[05:05] Jordan: "Good. For the pilot are you thinking Hosted first or straight to Dedicated/Private?"
[05:12] Marcus: "We prefer to validate with Hosted (fast) but if the security team signs off on BYOK we're open to Dedicated or Private. Cost is a concern though for steady-state."
[05:22] Priya: "Typical pattern we see: Hosted for fast iteration then move to Dedicated to control latency and cost once traffic is predictable; Private is chosen when regulators demand keys or full network isolation. For the pilot we can do a Hosted trial with BYOK and SAML to validate authentication and key flows."
[05:40] Sofia: "One more — encryption in transit. We need mTLS for internal RPCs and TLS for external endpoints. Is mTLS supported between components in Private?"
[05:48] Liam: "Yes — Private supports mTLS between control plane and worker nodes; we also support custom root CAs and mutual auth policies."
[06:00] Evelyn: "Can you walk through a concrete example — user calls the Hosted API, request hits Redwood, where are logs stored and how does KMS play in?"
[06:10] Priya: "Sure. Example trace: request -> endpoint (region pinned) -> auth (SAML/Token) -> route selection -> KV prefix cache check -> served from cache or executed on a worker -> output returned. Audit record contains request id, model id, route, timing, and optionally payload. Encryption: payload encrypted at rest with DEK, DEK wrapped by customer/master key in KMS. Logs stored per-tenant into configured sink; we redact payloads if configured."
[06:45] Marcus: "You mentioned KV cache — does caching introduce data leakage across tenants?"
[06:52] Priya: "No, caches are tenant-scoped. We use strict isolation keys and memory partitions. For Dedicated/Private you can have physical isolation on GPU worker pools."
[07:03] Evelyn: "About incident response — if there's a suspected breach, do you provide forensic exports and playbooks?"
[07:10] Jordan: "Yes, we have an incident playbook for customers: full export of audit logs, ephemeral access tokens, live session traces, and we can coordinate forensic collection through a designated SE or CSM. For enterprise customers there's a dedicated response SLA."
[07:25] Sofia: "Regulatory auditors sometimes ask for cryptographic proofs. You said a signed hash chain is an add-on — what's the proof format?"
[07:33] Priya: "A JSON lines export where each line has the audit event, timestamp, and signature. We provide the public verification key and sample verification code in Python. The chain uses HMAC-SHA256 with rotating signing keys, anchored to the customer KMS where possible."
[07:50] Marcus: "Cost question — when you store logs for 90 days + payloads, how does that factor into pricing?"
[07:57] Jordan: "Logging storage is either included up to a baseline (e.g., 30 days metadata) or charged for extended retention. We'll include storage cost in the pilot pricing and show a model. Also token-level billing is separate from storage."
[08:12] Evelyn: "About automated rollouts — can Redwood do canary traffic splitting and automatic rollback on quality regressions?"
[08:20] Priya: "Yes — rollouts support canary and A/B with automatic fallback to previous model if latency or error rate thresholds breach. We also integrate with eval hooks so you can run prompt-based regressions as part of CI for model rollouts."
[08:35] Sofia: "For Private deployments, how long does a typical on-prem install take?"
[08:40] Liam: "We have a standard on-prem bundle and a cloud-VPC package. On-prem (air-gapped with HSM) typically takes 6-8 weeks: network prep, HSM integration, smoke tests, and SOC/ops runbook handoff. VPC deployments are faster: usually 2-3 weeks if networking is ready."
[08:58] Marcus: "We have strict timeboxed windows for changes; what's the support model? 24/7?"
[09:03] Jordan: "Enterprise support tiers include 24/7 on-call and faster SLA for Dedicated/Private. We'll include SLA clauses in the pricing doc."
[09:11] Evelyn: "One technical nit — how do you handle token-level cost attribution when multiple teams share a Dedicated cluster? We need per-team billing exports."
[09:20] Priya: "We have token-level tagging and route-level cost attribution. You can tag requests with project IDs, and the console will break down cost by tag. We can also push breakdowns to your billing exports or billing integrations."
[09:35] Marcus: "Competitors have different story — some force you to migrate to their managed KMS; others don't offer signed audit chain. What do you think the tradeoffs are?"
[09:44] Jordan: "Tradeoff is ease vs control. Full manage simplifies onboarding but reduces control over keys. Our approach is to offer both: start managed for speed then bring your own KMS when needed."
[09:55] Sofia: "Ok next steps for us: get attestation docs and a sample perf run. We'll prep sample workload — mainly short chat-style prompts, average 150 tokens response, peak bursts to 1k tokens."
[10:07] Priya: "That helps — can you share token distribution and a sample payload? We'll run Dedicated vs Hosted baseline. Also please indicate if you require HSM-backed BYOK for the pilot."
[10:18] Marcus: "For the pilot, run Hosted with BYOK first. If results show issues, we'll move to Dedicated placement in our region."
[10:26] Jordan: "Noted. We'll schedule the benchmark. I'll send SOC2 and ISO docs and a deployment whitepaper. Priya will pick up the perf run and Liam will help sizing."
[10:35] Evelyn: "Two more quick items — VENDOR RISK: do you provide a shared responsibility matrix and pen-test reports?"
[10:42] Priya: "Yes, we have a vendor security pack with SOC2 report, ISO attestation, pen-test summary (redacted), and our shared responsibility matrix. We'll attach that."
[10:52] Sofia: "And SSO: do you support SCIM provisioning?"
[10:56] Liam: "Yes SCIM, group sync, and ephemeral SSO sessions. We can demo SCIM provisioning in the next call."
[11:05] Marcus: "Great. Anything else on compliance?"
[11:07] Evelyn: "We might ask for a third-party audit of the integration later but that's down the road."
[11:12] Jordan: "Understood. To recap, deliverables: SOC2/ISO docs, deployment whitepaper and diagram, signed audit log example, pilot pricing + timeline, run perf benchmark on sample workload (Hosted BYOK) and share results."
[11:28] Priya: "I'll own the perf run and the whitepaper. Jordan will cover pricing and legal pack. Sofia will share sample workload. Expect docs in 48 hours, benchmark week of 5/11."
[11:40] Marcus: "Works for us. Thank you. We'll review docs and get back with any gating questions."
[11:47] Jordan: "Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark deep dive. Recording and notes will be emailed."
[47:15] [call ends]

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Priya to send SOC2 attestation, ISO 27001 summary, pen-test highlights, and the deployment whitepaper (by 2026-05-07).
- Jordan to send pilot pricing and Dedicated commitment options (by 2026-05-08).
- Sofia to share anonymized sample workload and token distribution (by 2026-05-10).
- SE team to run Hosted-BYOK perf benchmark week of 2026-05-11 and present results.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — occasional mis-heard technical terms ("KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "samel" for SAML) and a few speaker attribution inconsistencies in the auto transcript; verified and corrected key action items manually.
